sam: Quick sync — ran a focused benchmark protocol + cold-start sweep this morning. High-level: synthetic replay parity breaks on KV-heavy traces; a kernel-shim change seems to have bumped short-seq p99. Putting numbers below and asking for triage ideas.

alex: Can you paste the exact harness commands and the model/config used?

sam: sure — harness: `./replay_harness --trace=kv_read_heavy.json --rate=1200rps --dist=poisson --duration=600`
model/config: `gpt-small-v2, kv_cache=enabled, batch_policy=auto, kernel_profile=fast-attn-v3, quant=none`

priya: Interesting. Did you run the same trace with synthetic generator (seq length & prompt mix matched)?

sam: yes — synthetic: `./synthetic_load --seq-dist=kv_match.json --rps=1200 --threads=48`
results diverge: replay p99 = 310ms, synthetic p99 = 220ms (short seq bucket). p50/p95 also slightly higher on replay.

jamie: Can you share profiling? flamegraph or perf summary?

sam: pasted profiling snippet from perf-agent run (cold path + warm):
```
cold-start (first 30s):
  - kernel-init: 42ms
  - alloc/kv-warm: 88ms
  - first-token-latency p99: 860ms
warm steady-state:
  - p50: 28ms
  - p95: 140ms
  - p99: 310ms
cpu/gpu breakdown (sampled):
  - attention-kernel: 45%
  - kv-serializing: 18%
  - scheduling overhead: 12%
```

sam: After applying the kernel-shim patch (r3145) we saw p99 for short sequences go from ~230ms -> ~310ms on replay harness; synthetic stayed ~220ms.

alex: kernel-shim patch touched work-queue ordering + alloc path, right? Could be causing KV cache warm races under replay speed.

priya: Also check batching heuristics: replay preserves real-world interarrival jitter which keeps smaller batches for short seqs; synthetic might coalesce more into larger batches, so kernel behavior differs. Did you force batching config to identical parameters?

sam: batching params were same on config file: `batch_max_size=32, batch_timeout_ms=8, dynamic_batching=true`. But replay interarrival distribution made mean batching size drop ~10%.

jamie: I ran a focused microbenchmark on KV serialization with and without the shim. Tiny script below:
```
for k in 100 1000 10000; do ./kv_bench --ops=$k --parallel=8 --kernel=fast-attn-v3 --shim=on; done
# results: shim on -> avg op latency +8-12% at small ops (<=1k)
```

infra-bot: benchmark-run completed: id=run-2026-03-17-09:12, nodes=8-gpu-a10g, harness=replay, duration=10m, artifact=/artifacts/run-2026-03-17-09-12.tgz

priya: That matches: KV serialization overhead compounds when batches are smaller (per-request amortization gone). If the shim added a micro-lock or ordering barrier, p99 for short seqs would increase.

alex: Are dedicated pools behaving differently? We saw previously that dedicated pools with higher burst credits mask short-term increases because they can spin up cached workers faster.

sam: On dedicated pool run: scale-up median 18s, cold-start median 420ms for first token; on shared-hosted bust we saw scale-up ~34s and first-token median 870ms. So dedicated helped but didn't remove the kernel reg.

jamie: I instrumented per-batch KV copy counts: shim on -> +1 copy per request in worst-case path (small batch). So that aligns.

priya: Proposed plan: (1) revert shim in canary and re-run replay harness across kv-heavy traces (2) add unit microbench for per-request KV copy counts (3) tweak batching timeout for replay to match synthetic batching size and re-evaluate apples-to-apples.

sam: I like. Also add flamegraph diff to PR so reviewers can see where the extra cycles show up.

alex: One more ask — include scale-up time vs sustained RPS curve. If the shim affects scheduler fairness, we might see increased contention during autoscale events.

sam: will run 3 runs: replay baseline, replay + shim, synthetic + shim. Each with dedicated and shared pool variants. I'll upload artifacts to the run above. ETA 6h.

jamie: If you want I'll review the perf artifacts live. Also suggest adding a probe that records per-request batch_size into traces so we can filter by actual batch size for p99.

sam: good idea — adding trace tag `batch_size` and `kv_copy_count`.

infra-bot: new-artifact uploaded: /artifacts/run-2026-03-17-09-12/kernels-flame-diff.txt

priya: If revert in canary fixes it, we should consider a micro-optimization to the shim rather than full revert — maybe move the lock to per-stream, or defer a copy until after scheduling.

alex: Agreed. Let's get data first. Sam please post a short summary when runs complete and mark any follow-up tickets. :thumbsup:

sam: will do — thanks all.
